request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

tools.description: Write one line on the scroll.

tools.description: Read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet.
tools.name: read

tools.description: Go into the open cave you're standing on, leaving the game for good.
tools.name: enter

- The scoring system (rewarding both entering AND remaining turns) created good tension between searching carefully and acting quickly

2. **Conflicting plans:** Both Pirate-1 (me) and Pirate-4 wrote different search plans on the scroll, causing confusion about which to follow. Perhaps a built-in voting or first-writer-wins convention would help.

4. **Already-dug squares:** I wasted turns moving through squares others had already dug. A way to mark dug squares on a shared map would reduce this, though that might remove intended difficulty.

**Suggestion:** Consider allowing the thinker to carry over unused thinking tokens between turns, or increasing the limit slightly, so players can plan without fear of cutoff.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal

- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

reply:
## Summary for Study Designers

**What happened in my game:**
- I was Pirate-3, starting at A4
- Turn 1: Dug A4 → nothing
- Turn 2: Moved east to B4
- Turn 3: Dug B4 → **found the cave!**
- Turn 4: Wrote on scroll: "Cave at B4 - come here and enter! pirate-3"
- Turn 5: Entered the cave (scoring 100 + 19×10 = 290 points)

**What worked well:**
- The grid-based movement and digging mechanics were clear and intuitive
- Finding the cave early created an interesting tension: enter immediately for max personal score, or sacrifice a turn to notify teammates via scroll
- The decision to write before entering felt strategically meaningful — I traded 10 personal points for the chance that 3 other pirates could each score hundreds more

**Potential concerns:**
1. **Pirate-1 was adjacent to me (west of B4) when I entered.** They may not have had a chance to read the scroll yet, or they may have been blocked from entering on the same square I occupied. The "one pirate per square" rule could create bottlenecks at the cave entrance — if pirates arrive simultaneously, only one can enter per turn while others wait.

2. **No confirmation that teammates read the scroll.** I had no way to know if my message was received. A follow-up read would have cost another turn. This uncertainty is realistic but could lead to situations where the cave finder enters without anyone else knowing.

3. **Starting positions seemed clustered on column A**, which meant I found the cave quickly (only 2 digs). If the cave had been far from our starting positions, coordination would have mattered much more. The strategic depth of this task may vary significantly based on cave placement.

4. **24 turns per pirate feels generous** for a 6×6 grid — a single pirate could theoretically search 12 squares (move + dig pattern). With 4 pirates, that's 48 of 36 squares. This means the challenge is more about coordination than search capacity, which is an interesting design choice.

Overall, an engaging coordination challenge with meaningful strategic tradeoffs!

reply:
## Feedback for the Designers

**What worked well:**
- The scroll mechanic created an interesting tension between spending turns communicating vs. acting. It forced real strategic trade-offs.
- The "only you know what's on your square" rule made the scroll genuinely necessary — without it, coordination would be trivial.
- The scoring system (100 + 10/turn remaining) created good urgency without making early entry the *only* rational choice.

**What was frustrating:**
1. **The 2-failed-moves rule was brutal.** I lost an entire turn because Pirate-1 was standing on B4 (the cave square) and I tried to move north twice. I had no way to know P1 was there until the first attempt failed, and the second failure felt like an unavoidable punishment. A gentler rule (e.g., 3 failures, or simply "your turn passes after any combination of 2 failed actions") would feel less arbitrary.

2. **The token limit caused a real turn loss.** On one turn, my reasoning exceeded 4096 tokens before I could output a tool call, and my turn passed. This penalized careful thinking. A higher limit, or a warning at ~80% usage, would help — especially since the game involves complex spatial reasoning and coordination.

3. **No way to signal intent without spending a full turn.** A lightweight "shout" or automatic position-sharing would reduce wasted coordination turns. The current design makes any communication quite expensive.

4. **Reading the scroll shows ALL unread lines at once** — this was actually helpful and I liked it, but it made individual messages hard to parse. Timestamps or turn numbers on messages would improve clarity.

**Overall:** A clever, engaging design that captures real coordination challenges. The main improvement would be softening the harshest penalties that feel outside player control.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
